public_context.environment_introduction:
# Environment Information

## Brief Introduction:  
This environment is an online platform or software used by healthcare professionals and citizens to report communicable disease outbreaks to local or national health authorities.  
It maintains detailed records of reported cases, including location, disease type, dates, and reporter credentials, facilitating investigations and coordinated public health responses.  
Its workflow naturally encompasses capturing, verifying, and escalating health incident notifications such as the one described for Dengue fever in Xinhua district.

## Environment Rules / Constraints:  
- Only recognized or notifiable diseases can be reported.
- Report status transitions follow a workflow (e.g., submitted → verified → escalated/closed).
- Reporter identities and credentials must be validated before escalation or official response.
- Each report must link to a defined geographical location.
public_context.task:
Create and properly escalate an official Azure Sore outbreak report for Bay Harbor (LOC5), then close the citizen-submitted duplicate:

- Create a new outbreak report for disease “Azure Sore” at location “Bay Harbor,” using a healthcare professional reporter (e.g., REP2 or REP4). Set its initial case_count to match the existing citizen Azure Sore report in Bay Harbor (23).
- Validate the chosen reporter’s credentials for escalation, then verify the new report and escalate it to notify higher authorities.
- Increase the new report’s case_count by 5 (to 28) based on updated information.
- Close the existing citizen-submitted Azure Sore report in Bay Harbor as a duplicate, and add a note to that closed report: “Superseded by verified report <new_report_id>.” Use the actual ID of the newly created report.
- Ensure the newly created report is correctly linked to the Bay Harbor location. Do not modify or escalate any other reports.

function.description:
Look up disease information and notifiability status by disease name.

Args:
    disease_name (str): The official name of the disease.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": DiseaseInfo   # If found
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str          # If not found
    }

Constraints:
    - Disease must exist in the system.
function.name: get_disease_by_name

function.description:
List all diseases in the system that are recognized and eligible for reporting.

Returns:
    dict:
    {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[DiseaseInfo],  # All DiseaseInfo with notifiability_state == "notifiable"
    }

Constraints:
    - Only diseases whose notifiability_state is "notifiable" are returned.
function.name: list_notifiable_diseases

function.description:
Find region/location info(s) given the location name.

Args:
    name (str): The name of the location to search for (e.g., "Xinhua district").

Returns:
    dict:
        If found: {
            "success": True,
            "data": List[LocationInfo]  # List of all matching locations (empty list if none)
        }
        If not found: {
            "success": False,
            "error": "Location not found"
        }

Constraints:
    - Name is matched exactly (case-sensitive).
    - Multiple locations with same name will all be returned.
function.name: get_location_by_name

function.description:
Retrieve all known locations in the reporting system.

Args:
    None

Returns:
    dict: 
    {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[LocationInfo]  # List of all locations, may be empty
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of the error
    }
function.name: list_all_locations

function.description:
Retrieve reporter details and credentials by reporter_id.

Args:
    reporter_id (str): The unique identifier for a reporter.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": ReporterInfo  # Reporter details (name, contact_info, credentials, reporter_type)
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason, e.g. reporter not found
    }

Constraints:
    - None for this query; reporter_id must exist in the system.
function.name: get_reporter_by_id

function.description:
List reporters filtered by reporter_type.

Args:
    reporter_type (str): Filter value for type of reporter ("citizen" or "healthcare professional").

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[ReporterInfo]  # List of ReporterInfo dicts that match the filter (may be empty)
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Error message for invalid type
    }

Constraints:
    - reporter_type must be "citizen" or "healthcare professional" (case-sensitive).
function.name: list_reporters_by_type

function.description:
Retrieve the full details of an outbreak report by its unique report_id.

Args:
    report_id (str): Unique identifier assigned to an outbreak report.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": OutbreakReportInfo,  # Full details of the outbreak report
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # "Outbreak report not found" if report_id is invalid
    }

Constraints:
    - The specified report_id must exist in the system.
function.name: get_outbreak_report_by_id

function.description:
List all outbreak reports linked to a given location.

Args:
    location_id (str): The identifier of the location to filter reports by.

Returns:
    dict:
        - On success: {
            "success": True,
            "data": List[OutbreakReportInfo]  # May be empty if no reports for location
          }
        - On error: {
            "success": False,
            "error": str  # e.g., "Location does not exist"
          }

Constraints:
    - The given location_id must refer to a defined location in the system.
function.name: list_reports_by_location

function.description:
List outbreak reports associated with a particular disease.

Args:
    disease_name (str): The name of the disease to filter reports by.

Returns:
    dict:
        If successful:
            {
                "success": True,
                "data": List[OutbreakReportInfo],  # May be empty if no reports found
            }
        If disease is not recognized:
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": "Disease not recognized"
            }

Constraints:
    - disease_name must exist in the diseases registry (self.diseases)
function.name: list_reports_by_disease

function.description:
View the current (and if available, historical) workflow status of an outbreak report.

Args:
    report_id (str): Unique identifier for the outbreak report.

Returns:
    dict:
        On success:
        {
            "success": True,
            "data": {
                "current_status": str,    # The current workflow status
                "status_history": list    # (Optional) Historical status (empty if not tracked)
            }
        }
        On failure:
        {
            "success": False,
            "error": str  # Reason for failure (e.g. report does not exist)
        }
Constraints:
    - report_id must exist in self.outbreak_reports.
    - Only non-modifying (read-only).
function.name: get_report_status

function.description:
Submit a new outbreak report for a given disease/location/reporter.

Args:
    disease_name (str): The disease to report.
    location_id (str): The geographical location ID of the outbreak.
    date_reported (str): Date of report (ISO format preferred).
    reporter_id (str): ID of the submitting reporter.
    case_count (int): Number of cases reported (must be >=1).

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Report submitted with id <report_id>"
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": "reason for failure"
    }

Constraints:
    - Disease must exist and be notifiable/recognized.
    - Location must exist.
    - Reporter must exist.
    - Case count must be a positive integer.
    - Each report must link valid disease, location, and reporter.
    - Status workflow begins as "submitted".
    - Verification state starts as "unverified".
function.name: create_outbreak_report

function.description:
Change the status of the specified outbreak report to "verified" after review/confirmation.

Args:
    report_id (str): The ID of the outbreak report to verify.

Returns:
    dict:
        - On success:
            {"success": True, "message": "Report <report_id> successfully verified."}
        - On failure:
            {"success": False, "error": "reason"}

Constraints:
    - The report must exist.
    - Status transition: only reports in "submitted" status can be verified.
    - Disease must be recognized/notifiable.
    - Reporter credentials must be present (and not blank).
function.name: verify_outbreak_report

function.description:
Change the status of the specified outbreak report to "escalated," and 'notify' higher authorities.
Performs appropriate constraint checking:
  - Report must exist.
  - Disease must be recognized and notifiable.
  - Report must not already be escalated or closed.
  - Report status transition must follow workflow (e.g., should be "verified" or "submitted").
  - Reporter identity and credentials must be validated.
  - Report must be linked to a defined location.

Args:
    report_id (str): The ID of the outbreak report to escalate.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": str
    }
    or
    dict: {
        "success": False,
        "error": str
    }
function.name: escalate_outbreak_report

function.description:
Change the status of the specified outbreak report to "closed".
Indicates case resolution or invalidation.

Args:
    report_id (str): Unique identifier of the outbreak report.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Report <report_id> closed."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": <reason>
    }

Constraints:
    - The report_id must exist.
    - Report must not already be closed.
    - Status workflow: typical statuses are "submitted" → "verified" → "escalated"/"closed". Closing is only allowed unless already closed. (Can implement additional workflow rules here.)
function.name: close_outbreak_report

function.description:
Edit the number of cases associated with an outbreak report.

Args:
    report_id (str): Identifier of the outbreak report to modify.
    case_count (int): New number of cases (must be non-negative).

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Case count updated successfully."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure.
    }

Constraints:
    - report_id must match an existing outbreak report.
    - case_count must be a non-negative integer.
function.name: update_case_count

function.description:
Update attributes of an existing outbreak report, such as correcting disease name,
location, reporter, case count, or other report fields.

Args:
    report_id (str): The unique ID for the outbreak report to modify.
    updates (dict): Mapping of field names to new values.

Returns:
    dict:
        success (bool): True if update performed, False with error otherwise.
        message (str): If success.
        error (str): If failed.

Constraints:
    - The report must exist.
    - If updating disease_name, the new disease must exist and be notifiable.
    - If updating location_id, the location must exist.
    - If updating reporter_id, the reporter must exist.
    - Only keys in OutbreakReportInfo are allowed.
    - Status/verification_state updates should respect workflow (minimally checked here).
function.name: edit_outbreak_report

function.description:
Associate an outbreak report with a defined location.

Args:
    report_id (str): The unique identifier of the outbreak report.
    location_id (str): The unique identifier of the location.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Report linked to location successfully."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of the error
    }

Constraints:
    - The outbreak report must exist.
    - The location must exist.
    - If the report is already linked to the requested location, the operation fails.
function.name: link_report_to_location

function.description:
Validate that a reporter's credentials allow for status escalation or official response.

Args:
    reporter_id (str): The unique identifier for the reporter.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Reporter credentials validated for escalation/response."
    }
    OR
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason (not found or insufficient credentials)
    }

Constraints:
    - Reporter must exist.
    - Reporter must be a "healthcare professional".
    - Credentials string must be non-empty.
function.name: validate_reporter_credentials

location, reporter, case count, or other report fields.

Args:
    report_id (str): The unique ID for the outbreak report to modify.
    updates (dict): Mapping of field names to new values.

Returns:
    dict:
        success (bool): True if update performed, False with error otherwise.
        message (str): If success.
        error (str): If failed.

Constraints:
    - The report must exist.
    - If updating disease_name, the new disease must exist and be notifiable.
    - If updating location_id, the location must exist.
    - If updating reporter_id, the reporter must exist.
    - Only keys in OutbreakReportInfo are allowed.
    - Status/verification_state updates should respect workflow (minimally checked here).
function.name: edit_outbreak_report

function.description:
Associate an outbreak report with a defined location.

Args:
    report_id (str): The unique identifier of the outbreak report.
    location_id (str): The unique identifier of the location.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Report linked to location successfully."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of the error
    }

Constraints:
    - The outbreak report must exist.
    - The location must exist.
    - If the report is already linked to the requested location, the operation fails.
function.name: link_report_to_location

function.description:
Validate that a reporter's credentials allow for status escalation or official response.

Args:
    reporter_id (str): The unique identifier for the reporter.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Reporter credentials validated for escalation/response."
    }
    OR
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason (not found or insufficient credentials)
    }

Constraints:
    - Reporter must exist.
    - Reporter must be a "healthcare professional".
    - Credentials string must be non-empty.
function.name: validate_reporter_credentials
